ann_33.text: Through this part, more vessels coloured raise a typical patient's predicted risk in an uneven way, from about 26% at 0 vessels to about 40% at 2 (on the training data only).
A thallium result coded 4 raises it here from about 26% to about 68% (on the training data only; the model has little data on this, 2 patients).

ann_34.text: This part acts on 47 of 242 training patients (19%), patients with a normal thallium scan; 22 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 63-year-old woman with no chest pain symptoms, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy and a normal thallium scan), it slightly raises the predicted risk, from about 1% to about 2% (on the training data only).
Through it, an abnormal thallium scan slightly lowers that patient's predicted risk, from about 2% to about 1% (on the training data only).

ann_35.text: This part acts on 110 of 242 training patients (45%); 81 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms, chest pain brought on by exercise, 1 vessel coloured, 1.4 mm of ST depression, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy, a flat ST segment and a reversible defect on the thallium scan), it clearly raises the predicted risk from about 94% to above 99%.
Through it, an abnormal thallium scan clearly raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 26% to about 67%.

An abnormal thallium scan and more ST depression clearly raise the predicted risk only if the patient does not have typical angina (to about 67% and about 65%, ST depression in an uneven way, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher; against no change at about 9% with typical angina).

More ST depression clearly raises it steadily, and even more so with an abnormal thallium scan (from about 29% to about 99%, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher, against about 26% to about 65%).

Through this part, ST depression adds to the predicted risk only once it rises above about 2.0 mm (for the typical patient with a fold, from about 5% to about 54%), and typical angina lowers the risk of the typical patient it acts on from above 99% to about 94% (on the training data only; the model has little data on the threshold).

ann_36.text: This part acts on 161 of 242 training patients (67%), patients without chest pain on exercise; 50 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 55-year-old man with non-anginal chest pain, no chest pain on exercise and a normal thallium scan), it lowers the predicted risk from about 12% to about 5% (on the training data only).

Through it, higher resting blood pressure lowers a typical patient's predicted risk, with nothing until about 108 mm Hg, then steadily, from about 47% at 110 to about 9% at 155 mm Hg; this holds for most patients, but for women it falls steadily over the whole range; being a woman lowers it to about 6%, and chest pain brought on by exercise raises it to about 49% (on the training data only).

Higher resting blood pressure clearly raises the predicted risk if exercise brings on chest pain, but the other way if it does not (from about 14% to about 57%, against about 26% to about 25%); for most patients it does so steadily, but for women it changes only beyond a point.

For men and patients without chest pain on exercise, resting blood pressure lowers the predicted risk through this part only once it rises above about 108 mm Hg (for the typical patient with a fold, from about 10% to about 1%; on the training data only).
Being a woman lowers the predicted risk slightly more without chest pain on exercise (from about 26% to about 1%, against about 29% to about 8% with it).

ann_37.text: This part acts on 82 of 242 training patients (34%), patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less, and 51 of them had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on (a 63-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms, 1 vessel coloured, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy, a flat ST segment and a reversible defect on the thallium scan), it slightly lowers the predicted risk, which stays at about 99% (on the training data only).

Through it, older age (42 to 66 years) lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 26% to about 16%, and for patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less only once age rises above about 61 years (on the training data only).

More vessels coloured raise it here in an uneven way, from about 26% at 0 vessels to about 40% at 2, while for two rare thallium results the model has little data on this: a fixed defect (15 patients) lowers it to below 1%, and a result coded 4 (2 patients) raises it to about 51% (on the training data only).

Each extra vessel coloured adds about the same, and clearly more for patients aged 56 or younger (from about 17% to about 89%, against about 33% to about 92%), flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher.

Older age clearly raises it more with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL (from about 2% to about 8%, against about 13% to about 27%), steadily for most patients, but for patients with a fixed defect on the thallium scan it is highest at one age and lower either side.

A fixed thallium defect lowers the predicted risk, and even more so with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less (from about 26% to about 2%, against about 5% to about 22% with higher fasting blood sugar). The model has little data on this: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).

ann_38.text: For a typical patient, the model clearly gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease with non-anginal chest pain (about 5%), typical angina (about 9%) or atypical angina (about 17%) than with no chest pain symptoms (about 26%).

More vessels coloured and higher cholesterol raise a typical patient's predicted risk steadily, from about 26% at 0 vessels to about 93% at 2 (flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher) and from about 16% at 193 mg/dL to about 45% at 308 mg/dL; a flat ST segment raises it to about 69%, and more ST depression raises it in an uneven way, mostly above about 2.0 mm, to about 65% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).

Being a woman lowers it to about 1%, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 5%, and a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 30% at 118 to about 23% at 175 beats per minute (on the training data only).
For two rare categories the model has little data on this: a thallium result coded 4 (2 patients; about 86%) and a downsloping ST segment (17 patients; about 16%), both on the training data only.
An ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG raises it only slightly, to about 29% (on the training data only; the model has little data on this, 2 patients).

ann_33.original: Affine ca relay (never clips on train): 148 = 0.555 + 0.181 ca + 0.234 thal:4. It adds +0.30 logit per ca SD to the output on top of the direct ca edge (total 1.63 logit/SD) and lowers the age-hinge threshold in 2034 for high ca. thal:4 (2 train rows) adds a small bump. Evidence: closed form; always active on 242/242 train rows; mean-ablation AUC 0.9605->0.9583. Evidence (train, n=242): 148 = relu(0.555 + 0.181 ca + 0.234 thal:4) on train: active on 242/242 rows (affine, never clips). 6 distinct values (5 ca levels + 2 thal:4 rows). Read out +1.658 to the logit (contrib SD 0.475) and +0.906 into 2034. Effective direct ca slope = 1.331 + 1.658*0.181 = 1.63 logit/SD. Mean-ablation: train AUC 0.9605 -> 0.9583, 3 prediction flips.
ann_33.proposed: A relay through which more vessels coloured raise the predicted risk.

ann_34.original: Binary indicator of normal thal (thal=3): 0.843 if normal, 0 otherwise (verified on all 242 train rows). Feeds 2034 at -0.578, raising the age threshold of the age hinge for normal-thal patients by ~0.52 age SD. Evidence (train, n=242): 7566 = relu(1.067 thal:3 - 0.107): on train takes exactly two values, 0.843 when thal=3 (normal, 135 rows) and 0 otherwise (107 rows); active pattern equals thal:3 exactly.
ann_34.proposed: A normal-thallium-scan indicator with only a slight effect on the predicted risk.

ann_35.original: Thal-defect x oldpeak gate. For patients with an abnormal thallium scan (fixed or reversible defect) and chest pain other than typical angina, it is always on and affine: +2.37 logit offset plus +2.51 logit per oldpeak SD. For normal thal, it is off unless oldpeak exceeds +0.81 SD (11/123 train rows). Typical angina (cp:1) shifts it down by 1.76 logit. It carries the network's main thal effect (mean +3.0 logit abnormal vs +0.16 normal) and makes oldpeak matter far more with a thal defect. Most important hidden unit: mean-ablation train AUC 0.9605->0.9187. Evidence (train, n=242): 2985 = relu(-0.373 - 1.008 cp:1 + 1.438 oldpeak - 1.253 thal:3), read out +1.749 (logit contrib SD 2.38, largest single term). Train: abnormal thal & cp!=1: active 97/97 (affine, pre = 1.35 + 1.44 oldpeak); abnormal thal & cp=1: 2/10; normal thal & cp!=1: 11/123 (hinge at oldpeak > +0.81 SD); normal thal & cp=1: 0/12. Mean logit contribution: abnormal thal +3.00, normal thal +0.16. Sensitivity (train): cp:1 0.45, oldpeak 0.65, thal:3 0.56. Mean-ablation AUC 0.9605 -> 0.9187, 37 flips (28 previously correct). No other path carries thal:3 to the output except via 7566->2034.
ann_35.proposed: A thallium-defect and ST-depression part acting on 110 patients: an abnormal thallium scan raises the predicted risk and makes ST depression raise it more, but neither matters with typical angina.

ann_36.original: Protective no-exercise-angina gate (read out -0.678). On for patients without exercise-induced angina (all women, 96% of men), off for men with exercise angina; contributes -1.78 logit on average without angina (larger for women: -2.68) and ~0 with it. While on, its trestbps term cancels the direct trestbps edge, so resting blood pressure only raises predicted risk for patients with exercise angina (net +0.84 logit/SD) and has ~zero net effect otherwise. Evidence: closed form, stratified activation on train, sensitivity, mean-ablation AUC 0.9605->0.9409. Evidence (train, n=242): 791 = relu(0.474 + 1.006 sex:0 - 0.151 sex:1 + 1.276 trestbps + 2.323 exang:0 - 0.559 exang:1), read out -0.678. Train active fractions: female no-exang 64/64 (mean 3.95), male no-exang 92/96 (mean 1.75), female exang 5/19, male exang 0/63. Mean logit contribution: no exercise angina -1.78, exercise angina -0.06. When on, trestbps slope -0.678*1.276 = -0.866 cancels the direct +0.838 edge. Sensitivity (train): exang:0 1.57, trestbps 0.86, sex:0 0.68. Mean-ablation AUC 0.9605 -> 0.9409, 20 flips.
ann_36.proposed: A part acting on patients without chest pain on exercise that lowers their predicted risk; through it, resting blood pressure above about 108 mm Hg lowers the risk, so resting blood pressure raises the risk only with chest pain on exercise.

ann_37.original: Serial composition of ca_relay and normal_thal_flag into an age hinge for patients with normal fasting blood sugar. 2034 switches on above an age threshold that depends on thal (fixed defect: always; reversible defect: ~+0.3 SD; normal: ~+0.8 SD) and drops with ca; it never fires when fbs>120. Once on it subtracts 1.39 logit per age SD, reversing the direct age slope (+0.56) to -0.82, i.e. among older, normal-sugar, abnormal-thal patients the model predicts slightly less risk with age, matching a negative age-outcome correlation in that train subgroup (r=-0.12, n=82). Modest effect (AUC 0.9605->0.9484 when mean-ablated); plausibly a fit to this subgroup rather than a clinical mechanism. Evidence (train, n=242): 2034 = relu(-1.014 + 0.944 age + 1.407 fbs:0 + 0.793 thal:6 + 0.906*ca_relay - 0.578*normal_thal_flag), read out -1.469. Train: active 82/242; 0/33 with fbs>120. Age-SD thresholds (fbs normal, ca=0): normal thal +0.83, reversible defect +0.31, fixed defect -3.2 (always on); each ca level lowers the threshold ~0.2 SD. Past the hinge, logit slope in age = 0.563 (direct) - 1.469*0.944 = -0.82/SD. Empirically corr(age, y) is -0.12 among the 82 active rows vs +0.23 among inactive rows, consistent with the reversal. Mean contrib among active -1.40 (min -6.92). Mean-ablation AUC 0.9605 -> 0.9484; zeroing it flips 6 predictions (4 previously correct).
ann_37.proposed: A part acting on 82 patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less: through it, age above about 61 years lowers the predicted risk and more vessels raise it.

ann_38.original: Additive composition at the logit: a 15-term linear model plus four hidden corrections, then sigmoid. Unlike a plain logistic regression, thal has no direct edge: it acts only through thal_defect_oldpeak (abnormal thal: +3 logit and steep oldpeak slope) and the age hinge. no_angina_bp_gate subtracts risk without exercise angina and makes BP matter only with it. older_normal_fbs_age_hinge flattens/reverses the age effect for older normal-sugar patients with abnormal thal. ca_relay is an affine boost to the ca weight. Hidden units carry substantial signal: mean-ablating all of them drops train AUC from 0.960 to 0.870. cp:2, restecg:0, restecg:2 and thal:7 are unconnected, zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, n=242): Root logit = -0.586 + direct linear terms (SD 2.84) + 1.658*ca_relay (SD 0.48) - 0.678*no_angina_bp_gate (SD 1.21) + 1.749*thal_defect_oldpeak (SD 2.38) - 1.469*older_normal_fbs_age_hinge (SD 1.09); total logit SD 4.61. Train AUC 0.9605, acc 0.897. Mean-ablating all four readout hidden nodes: AUC 0.870. Largest direct weights (per SD): ca 1.33, slope:2 1.08, trestbps 0.84, sex:1 0.71, fbs:1 -0.68, chol 0.62, cp:3 -0.59, age 0.56. Inputs cp:2, restecg:0, restecg:2, thal:7 have no edges (zero effect); thal enters only via hidden units.
ann_38.proposed: Any chest pain type, being a woman, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL and a higher maximum heart rate lower the predicted risk; more vessels, a flat ST segment, more ST depression and higher cholesterol raise it. An abnormal thallium scan raises it only without typical angina, and resting blood pressure raises it only with chest pain on exercise.

summary.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk of heart disease about 26%), the model clearly gives a lower predicted risk with non-anginal chest pain (about 5%), typical angina (about 9%) or atypical angina (about 17%).

More vessels coloured by fluoroscopy and higher cholesterol raise a typical patient's predicted risk steadily, from about 26% at 0 vessels to about 93% at 2 (flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher) and from about 16% at 193 mg/dL to about 45% at 308 mg/dL; a flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 69%, and more ST depression on exercise raises it in an uneven way, mostly above about 2.0 mm, to about 65% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).
Being a woman lowers it to about 1%, and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 5% (on the training data only).

An abnormal thallium scan clearly raises the predicted risk, but only if the patient does not have typical angina: from about 26% to about 67% without typical angina, and no change (about 9%) with it.

More ST depression clearly raises the predicted risk steadily, and even more so with an abnormal thallium scan: from about 29% to about 99%, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher, against about 26% to about 65% with a normal scan.

Higher resting blood pressure clearly raises the predicted risk if exercise brings on chest pain, but the other way if it does not: for most patients steadily, but for women it changes only beyond a point, going from about 14% at 110 mm Hg to about 57% at 155 mm Hg with chest pain on exercise, and from about 26% to about 25% without it.

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients

ann_33.text: Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if thallium stress test result coded 4 (meaning not recorded) applies (about 68%) than if thallium stress test result is something other than thallium stress test result coded 4 (meaning not recorded) (about 26%) (on the training data only). The model has little data on this: only 2 training patients (thallium stress test result coded 4 (meaning not recorded)).

Through this part, the model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease in an uneven way: for a typical patient, it goes from about 26% at 0 vessels to about 40% at 2 vessels (on the training data only).

ann_34.text: This part acts on 47 of 242 training patients (19%); nearly all of them are patients with a normal thallium scan.
For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 1% without this part to about 2% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 22 of these 47 patients had heart disease.

Through this part, for a typical patient this part acts on, the model gives a slightly lower predicted risk of heart disease if thallium stress test result is something other than a normal thallium scan (about 1%) than if the thallium scan is normal (about 2%) (on the training data only).

ann_35.text: This part acts on 110 of 242 training patients (45%).
For a typical patient it acts on, it clearly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 94% without this part to above 99% with it.
In the training data, 81 of these 110 patients had heart disease.
